newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Kepco posts lowest bid for Manila project.
newsitem.headline: Kepco posts lowest bid for Manila project.

text.p: The Philippines' National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday Korea Electric Power Co (Kepco) was the lowest bidder among six groups which vied for the 1,200-megawatt power plant to be built in Ilijan, Batangas, south of Manila.
Napocor president Guido A. Delgado said the Napocor board had approved the start of negotiations with Kepco for the build-operate-transfer (BOT) contract to put up the plant.

The power firm opened last Friday the financial bids of six bidders namely Marubeni Corp with Sithe Energy; Korea Electric Power Corp ; Ilijan Power Corp led by Enron Corp ; PowerGen Plc with Siemens AG ; Consolidated Electric Power Asia with Mitsubishi Corp; and the consortium of Alsons Power Holdings-Tomen Corp -Singapore Power Inc (SPI).
"We are extremely pleased with the results of this bid particularly because the partial government guarantee means a reduced liability for the Philippine Republic," Delgado said.
Kepco submitted a bid which required partial government guarantee while four of the six groups sought full government guarantee.
Delgado said Alsons-Tomen-SPI submitted the second lowest bid, followed by Cepa-Mitsubishi.
